title: Andy Dunn’s startup Pie evolves from an events app to a social networking platform
summary: Pie, a startup founded by Andy Dunn (Bonobos founder), has transitioned from an events-focused app to a social networking platform with its new 'Community Homes' feature. The update aims to foster real-world connections by allowing users to create permanent digital spaces for social groups, moving beyond single-event interactions. The app now emphasizes community-building, with tools like group feeds, admin controls, and casual connection prompts. Pie has grown to 300,000 users and targets younger audiences seeking in-person interactions post-pandemic. The shift reflects a broader cultural trend toward real-life social clubs and deeper community engagement.
key_points: Pie was originally an events app but now focuses on social networking with 'Community Homes' for group interactions.
The new feature allows users to create permanent digital spaces for social groups, replacing tools like group texts or Facebook Groups.
Community Homes include group feeds, admin controls, shareable homepages, and event planning resources.
Future updates will add group chats and casual connection prompts (e.g., 'hang out and craft together').
Pie’s pivot follows user behavior shifts, with time spent on the app increasing from 2 to 10 minutes after prioritizing social connections over events.
The app has 300,000 users and traction in cities like Chicago, New York, and Los Angeles.
Inspired by Gen Z’s interest in social clubs (e.g., run clubs, art markets), Pie positions itself as a 'Reddit for IRL' (in real life).
Co-founder Nadya Okamoto (founder of Zoomies run club) describes Pie as fulfilling the original promise of Facebook/Reddit without anonymity or toxicity.
